correctness.rationale: For u=x/b the left fixed-point equation is h_b(u)=1−a, h_b(u)=(1−bu)/cos(πu/2). Its derivative numerator Q_b goes from −b to (π/2)(1−b), and Q'_b=(π²/4)(1−bu)cos(πu/2)>0. Thus h_b drops from 1 to its unique minimum m_b and increases to infinity, giving exactly the advertised intersections for levels in (0,1). Reflection of the interior fixed-point equations gives c=h_(1−b)((1−x)/(1−b)), not a global conjugacy of the discontinuous map. The endpoints and assigned switch value are not fixed. Both interior branches have positive multipliers. Strict convexity/concavity of F−x gives the stated ordering of slopes in the two-root cases, and at tangency F'=1, F''≠0 and the respective a or c derivative is a positive cosine. At the left fold the displacement is positive on either side, so it attracts from the left and repels to the right locally; the signs reverse at the right fold. Evaluating h at the previous minimizer proves strict decrease of m_b in b; h_1(u)=(1−u)/sin((π/2)(1−u))>2/π, and continuity at each fixed u<1 followed by u→1 gives the limiting minimum 2/π. The implicit root near (b,u)=(0,0) is analytic and odd in b because Q_(−b)(−u)=−Q_b(u), so u_b=4b/π²+O(b³) and m_b=1−2b²/π²+O(b⁴); reflection gives the other endpoint law. The exact rational witness follows from 3·297²=264627>250000=500², testing x=1/6 and 5/6 and the branch ends. This proves the closed census on the stated open parameter cube, all-breakpoint coexistence, and local stability, not full basins or higher periods. The deposited verifier was inspected, not executed; its finite grid is supplemental.
